phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ra. These are the verses of the Book. What has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe
phrases.explanation: The separate letters open the chapter, and many early commentators left their exact meaning to Allah while reciting them as revelation. What follows is named verses of the Book, then the Quran given to Muhammad is declared truth while most people do not believe. That final clause sets the social weather for the whole chapter, because signs in sky, earth, womb, storm, and history will still meet readers who prefer a different conclusion.

phrases.translation: It is Allah Who has raised the heavens without pillars—as you can see—then established Himself on the Throne.
phrases.explanation: Heavens raised without pillars you can see uses a visible absence as an argument, because no props hold the sky in the way a tent or roof requires. Early explanation also allowed pillars not seen, while the Quranic emphasis stays on a lifted order resting in divine power. Established on the Throne joins that power with rule. The reader is invited to look upward and then beyond sight to the management that makes the view possible.

phrases.translation: He has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term.
phrases.explanation: Sun and moon subjected and each running to an appointed term places the most reliable clocks inside mortality. They serve human fasting, agriculture, travel, and calendars, yet their racetrack has an end appointed by the One who enrolled them. Subjects do not become gods merely by being useful and majestic. The verse demotes the brightest bodies into employees of an order, teaching worshippers to thank the manager rather than the instruments.

phrases.translation: He conducts the whole affair. He makes the signs clear so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord
phrases.explanation: He conducts the affair and explains signs so people may be certain of meeting their Lord turns astronomy into resurrection evidence. Detailed management now implies an appointment later, since a life inside a conducted universe should expect its conductor to settle its meaning. Certainty is the intended fruit rather than mere information. The heavens are not displayed to make a person feel small for entertainment. They are arranged to make the final meeting feel intellectually near.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who spread out the earth and placed firm mountains and rivers upon it,
phrases.explanation: Earth spread out with firm mountains and rivers gives the travelling reader a ground level counterpart to the raised heavens. Mountains are repeatedly pictured as stabilising weights in the Quran, while rivers cut routes of life through otherwise severe terrain. Human settlement depends on both durable height and moving water. A person can cross the evidence on foot, drinking from it and camping under it, without needing a temple lecture to begin reflection.

phrases.translation: and created fruits of every kind in pairs.
phrases.explanation: Fruits made in pairs extends design into reproduction and variety across orchards and fields. Early commentators discussed male and female in plants, kinds and opposites, sweet and sour, and the broad pairing found in creation. The verse need not be squeezed into one botanical detail to perform its work. Food reaches the table through patterns people did not invent, and appetite becomes an occasion to notice a producer beyond the farmer hands.

phrases.translation: He covers the day with night. Surely in this are signs for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: Night covers day like a garment drawn over light, reversing the visible order every evening without human permission. Surely in that are signs for people who reflect makes thought the bridge between scenery and worship. Reflection here is a habit of tracing gift to giver and order to commander while the evidence is still ordinary. A reader can watch the same dusk as a neighbour and either catalogue colours or hear a summons.

phrases.translation: And on the earth there are ˹different˺ neighbouring tracts, gardens of grapevines, ˹various˺ crops, palm trees—some stemming from the same root, others standing alone.
phrases.explanation: Neighbouring tracts, vineyards, crops, and date palms either sharing a root cluster or standing separately form a compact agricultural parable. Soil can change across a boundary stone while vines, grain, and palms ask different things from the same farmer. Clustered and single palms may share a source or stand alone, yet neither arrangement decides flavour by itself. The verse sets diversity inside closeness so lazy explanations from environment alone will not finish the work.

phrases.translation: They are all irrigated with the same water, yet We make some taste better than others.
phrases.explanation: One water irrigates them all while some are favoured over others in taste gives the central riddle. Same rain can produce sweet Dates, sour fruit, nourishing grain, and bitter growth because natures and soils receive it differently. Commentators often drew the moral parallel to human hearts under one revelation. A uniform gift does not guarantee a uniform result, which helps explain why identical signs create certainty in one person and argument in another.

phrases.translation: Surely in this are signs for those who understand
phrases.explanation: Signs for people who reason ends the field scene by naming the faculty required to move from flavour to meaning. Taste buds can register difference without asking why sameness of water did not erase distinction. Reason in the Quran is practical and moral, not a cold machine detached from gratitude. It notices how receptors matter, then turns the lesson inward before blaming a message for the condition of the soil receiving it.

phrases.translation: ˹Now,˺ if anything should amaze you ˹O Prophet˺, then it is their question:
phrases.explanation: If you wonder, the real wonder is their saying reframes astonishment before the resurrection objection is even quoted. A prophet may marvel at people who accept seeds reviving and babies forming while treating a returned body as impossible. The sentence does not mock the Prophet. It tells him where amazement belongs. Denial can sound sophisticated until its ordinary surroundings are allowed to cross examine it.

phrases.translation: “When we are reduced to dust, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
phrases.explanation: When we are dust shall we be in a new creation puts the decayed corpse at the centre of the argument. Dust feels like evidence of final dispersal to people watching bodies vanish into soil. The Quran repeatedly answers from first creation and seasonal revival because the God who assembled a body from earthly materials is not defeated by their later mixture. Dust is therefore less an ending than a familiar ingredient in the divine workshop.

phrases.translation: It is they who have disbelieved in their Lord. It is they who will have shackles around their necks.
phrases.explanation: Those are the ones who disbelieve in their Lord and have shackles on their necks turns intellectual denial into bondage. A shackle can picture final punishment while also suggesting the present grip of a chosen error around movement. People may feel free because nobody can compel belief, yet a premise that forces every sign into denial can become its own chain. The verse names the destination of a thought after it has governed a life.

phrases.translation: And it is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: Residents of the Fire forever ends the contrast between a temporary grave in dust and a permanent settlement after return. The very people who said a new creation is impossible are promised a lasting existence they did not budget for. Forever carries force because resurrection will place them beyond the decay they trusted as escape. The verse therefore preaches from their own dust, saying matter can be gathered for judgment as surely as it was gathered for birth.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ to hasten the torment rather than grace, though there have ˹already˺ been ˹many˺ torments before them.
phrases.explanation: They ask you to hasten evil before good while exemplary punishments have already passed before them gives mockery a history lesson. Ruined peoples from earlier chapters are the passed examples, visible enough that demanding a fresh one looks reckless. Hastening punishment can sound brave in a debate where the sky stays calm during the sentence. The verse asks why a person would request the finishing event of the argument while time for change remains available.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is full of forgiveness for people, despite their wrongdoing, and your Lord is truly severe in punishment
phrases.explanation: Your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing places an open gate directly beside their dare. The same Lord is severe in punishment, so patience must not be misread as softness about evil. Holding both names in one breath keeps the preacher from becoming only threatening or only soothing. Human beings are allowed time because forgiveness is real, and warned about time because severity is equally real when rejection becomes the settled fruit.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “If only a sign could be sent down to him from his Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Why is no sign sent down to him from his Lord means a sign on their chosen terms after heavens, earth, womb, and revelation have already been placed around them. A request can hide refusal when each supplied sign is reclassified as ordinary, literary, or insufficiently theatrical. The verse prepares the Prophet for a demand that will not necessarily end if another wonder appears. Audiences can use criteria as moving fences to keep surrender outside.

phrases.translation: You ˹O Prophet˺ are only a warner. And every people had a guide
phrases.explanation: You are only a warner and every people had a guide defines both Muhammad role and a universal pattern. A warner delivers the danger and the road away from it. He does not manufacture the acceptance of an audience or schedule every miracle demanded in council. Guides across peoples also mean the present audience is not uniquely neglected. Their request enters a long queue of nations who thought a custom sign might spare them the cost of listening.

phrases.translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what increases and decreases in the wombs.
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what every female carries turns from vast skies to the hidden interior of pregnancy, where sex, number, condition, and future are folded away from public sight. Wombs decreasing and increasing was explained through the stages and terms of gestation, miscarriage, blood, development, and what grows or falls short in ways known fully only to God. A community can count months approximately. Exact life inside the body remains a parable of knowledge held without announcement.

phrases.translation: And with Him everything is determined with precision
phrases.explanation: Everything with Him is by measure gives the womb verse a universal ruler. Measure includes quantity, timing, limit, and appointed outcome across embryo, rainfall, lifespan, kingdom, and revelation. The world is not chaos with occasional religious decoration. It is measured at depths human instruments approach only partly. For a prophet facing demands for instant signs, measure also means God will not be rushed out of a schedule already fitted to wisdom.

phrases.translation: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the seen and the unseen—the All-Great, Most Exalted
phrases.explanation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great and Most High, gathers the womb, heavens, private plots, and final meeting into one knowledge. Witnessed things are not more real to Allah because people can point at them. Unseen things are not dim because human senses have yet to invent a path. Greatness and exaltation prevent this knowledge from sounding like surveillance by a merely bigger creature. The One who knows every layer also stands above every pressure.

phrases.translation: It is the same ˹to Him˺ whether any of you speaks secretly or openly,
phrases.explanation: Secret speech and public speech are the same before Him because volume is a property for ears in a room, not a barrier for divine hearing. A conspirator can lower a voice and feel that meaning has become safer. The verse dissolves that comfort without requiring an angel at every wall in the imagination. Speech begins as intention and sound in a universe already known, so privacy is a human courtesy rather than a region outside God.

phrases.translation: whether one hides in the darkness of night or goes about in broad daylight
phrases.explanation: Hiding by night and moving openly by day also stand level in that knowledge. Night in the chapter will soon carry clouds, lightning, fear, and hope, so darkness is no separate kingdom. A person planning wrong after sunset and a person worshipping before dawn are equally seen. That equality can frighten plotters and console the lonely righteous at the same time. The verse is therefore a lock on secret evil and a lamp for secret good.

phrases.translation: For each one there are successive angels before and behind, protecting them by Allah’s command.
phrases.explanation: Successive guards before and behind every person are understood as angels who protect and record by Allah command, with shifts by night and day in familiar reports. Protection here is a delegated care rather than independent partnership. Being surrounded in front and behind makes the road feel attended for people who imagine themselves unobserved except by rivals. It also means a deed whispered into darkness meets a record before any human archive wakes.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah would never change a people’s state ˹of favour˺ until they change their own state ˹of faith˺.
phrases.explanation: Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is in themselves makes inner condition the hinge of public fortune. Early readings focused especially on God not removing a favour until a people replace gratitude and obedience with rebellion. The sentence does not ignore invasion, economics, weather, or leadership. It locates a moral source under national weather, telling communities that the first repair shop is the heart and conduct of the population itself.

phrases.translation: And if it is Allah’s Will to torment a people, it can never be averted, nor can they find a protector other than Him
phrases.explanation: If Allah wills harm for a people there is no turning it back and no guardian besides Him states the limit once inward change has ripened into decree. The same Lord who delays for change becomes the only possible shelter when consequences arrive. This prevents the previous line from becoming a self help promise that technique can force heaven into favourable weather. A people need inner reform sought under the Guardian, not public relations against Him.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who shows you lightning, inspiring ˹you with˺ hope and fear, and produces heavy clouds
phrases.explanation: He shows you lightning as fear and hope while constructing heavy clouds, giving the chapter its name through the storm world about to be praised. Lightning can frighten travellers and promise rain to farmers in the same flash, so one sign teaches two directions of the heart. Heavy clouds carry visible weight in the sky, tons of water suspended over fields without a warehouse roof. The verse trains readers to read weather theologically without pretending meteorology makes God unnecessary.

phrases.translation: The thunder glorifies His praises, as do the angels in awe of Him.
phrases.explanation: Thunder glorifies praise in the language of the scene, whether early readers pictured thunder itself, an angel charged with clouds, or the sound functioning as a sign that calls hearers to glorify. Angels also glorify from fear, joining seen weather with unseen worship. The verse refuses to let a storm be morally mute. Its noise drives some people under roofs and into prayer while others argue through the shaking windows.

phrases.translation: He sends thunderbolts, striking with them whoever He wills. Yet they dispute about Allah. And He is tremendous in might
phrases.explanation: Thunderbolts sent to strike whom He wills while human beings dispute about Allah gives the argument a violent backdrop. A bolt can find a tree, a tower, or a person with a precision no debating council controls. Severe in might ends the verse by naming the power behind both sound and strike. The irony is sharp, because creatures can be arguing about sovereignty while standing on ground that one flash can mark without asking their theory.

phrases.translation: Calling upon Him ˹alone˺ is the truth. But those ˹idols˺ the pagans invoke besides Him ˹can˺ never respond to them in any way.
phrases.explanation: The call of truth belongs to Allah because He is the real object and answerer of ultimate invocation. Beings called besides Him respond with nothing, a silence repeated at shrines, vows, storms, childbirth, sickness, and battle. This nothing is not mere delay. It is incapacity built into the address. The verse sets up an experiment anyone can observe in ordinary desperation when invented helpers need human attendants to speak for them.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ just like someone who stretches out their hands to water, ˹asking it˺ to reach their mouths, but it can never do so.
phrases.explanation: Stretching hands toward water so it may rise to the mouth gives false prayer a physical theatre. The person makes the shape of asking while refusing the motion that drink requires, or calls water from a distance that cannot obey a voice. Commentators pictured a man at a well or reaching toward a mirage like pool. Either image exposes effort aimed at an object unable to cooperate with hope.

phrases.translation: The calls of the disbelievers are only in vain
phrases.explanation: The call of disbelievers is only in error gathers the silent idols and the unreached water into one diagnosis. Error can include wasted direction and lost outcome rather than just mistaken vocabulary. A whole life of sincere appeals may need its address corrected before its intensity becomes benefit. The verse is severe toward the system and practical toward the person, because thirst is real even when the chosen well is a picture.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and the earth—willingly or unwillingly—as do their shadows, morning and evening
phrases.explanation: Everything in heavens and earth prostrates to Allah willingly or unwillingly, and shadows do so morning and evening, making even absence of light trace obedience across the ground. Believers bow in love while created things submit by constitution, and resistant people still live inside hunger, gravity, illness, ageing, and death. Shadows lengthening and shrinking become daily calligraphy of dependence. The human problem is not whether a body participates in divine order. It is whether the heart consents.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?”
phrases.explanation: Who is Lord of heavens and earth begins a guided interrogation rather than an information request. Say Allah supplies the answer the audience already accepts, so later questions can expose inconsistency instead of importing a new premise. The Prophet is told to answer when evasive silence might prolong the scene. Starting from a shared Lord makes the next charge harder to dismiss as foreign theology. It is their own admission placed under a lamp.

phrases.translation: Say, “Allah!” Ask ˹them˺, “Why ˹then˺ have you taken besides Him lords who cannot even benefit or protect themselves?”
phrases.explanation: Why take protectors besides Him who possess neither benefit nor harm even for themselves turns helper language against the helpers. A being requiring cleaning, guarding, feeding through offerings, repair, and priests cannot supply independent benefit at the ultimate level. Even for themselves is the cut, since a protector who needs protection from weather and thieves has reversed the job description. The verse makes voters inspect the strength of the candidates they appoint over fear.

phrases.translation: Say, “Can the blind and the sighted be equal? Or can darkness and light be equal?”
phrases.explanation: Can blind and seeing be equal or darkness and light be equal turns faculties and environments into two quick tests. A person may respect a blind neighbour deeply while still not assigning him to read a distant signal. Darkness and light can occupy the same road at different hours yet never perform the same work. The analogies ask whether worship of the seeing Lord and worship of unseeing partners can ever be flattened by social courtesy.

phrases.translation: Or have they associated with Allah partners who ˹supposedly˺ produced a creation like His, leaving them confused between the two creations?
phrases.explanation: Have they made partners who created like His creation so creation became confused to them asks for the exhibit that justifies a tie. Confusion should have a cause in comparable output if two makers truly stood side by side. No partner mountain, womb, storm, pair of fruits, or resurrected body can be produced. The question allows the possibility only long enough for the empty display shelf to become visible.

phrases.translation: Say, “Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Supreme.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is Creator of everything and the One, the Irresistible concludes from shared lordship, failed helpers, unequal faculties, and missing rival creation. Everything leaves no unowned corner where a partner could be manufacturer rather than product. Irresistible or Supreme completes the picture with authority that cannot be outvoted by a council of statues. The verse becomes a compact courtroom argument ending in worship instead of applause.

phrases.translation: He sends down rain from the sky, causing the valleys to flow, each according to its capacity.
phrases.explanation: He sent water from the sky and valleys flowed according to measure gives revelation a landscape in which capacity decides visible volume. A wide wadi carries a river while a narrow channel carries a stream from the same rain system. Early application naturally compares hearts receiving guidance in different measures. The rain is not blamed when a shallow passage cannot hold a flood. Geography makes receptivity visible without reducing people to dirt alone.

phrases.translation: The currents then carry along rising foam, similar to the slag produced from metal that people melt in the fire for ornaments or tools.
phrases.explanation: Torrent carrying swelling foam introduces the bright, noisy surface that will represent falsehood as it rides above useful water. Foam looks large because it gathers air, debris, and speed at the top. Metal heated for ornaments or tools produces a similar scum when the valuable material separates under fire. Two workshops of daily life, street rain and a smelter bench, now hold the same moral shape before the verse names it.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah compares truth to falsehood. The ˹worthless˺ residue is then cast away, but what benefits people remains on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Thus Allah presents truth and falsehood makes the parable explicit after the eye has learned its grammar. Foam disappears as scum, while what benefits people from water and purified metal remains in the earth for use. Public prominence is therefore a poor judge of permanence. A noisy idea may billow above a flood for one season, and a useful truth may look quiet at the bottom, yet time sorts weight from froth.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah sets forth parables
phrases.explanation: Thus Allah sets forth parables closes by honouring analogy as a teaching method rather than decoration after doctrine. A farmer, metalworker, child at a flooded path, and city official can all enter the same verse through work they know. Parables also protect truth from being trapped in an argument only specialists can repeat. When later crowds foam, a reader has a wadi in memory against which to measure them.

phrases.translation: Those who respond to ˹the call of˺ their Lord will have the finest reward.
phrases.explanation: Those who answer their Lord receive the finest reward, a word that can include Paradise and every good by which God outgives obedience. Answering turns revelation into a conversation rather than weather heard through a wall. The finest stands deliberately after the foam image because lasting benefit belongs to the substance that remained. A person who answers early may look less visible than the foam, yet duration will reverse the apparent ranking.

phrases.translation: As for those who do not respond to Him, even if they were to possess everything in the world twice over,
phrases.explanation: If those who do not answer possessed all earth and its like with it imagines the largest possible bank account at judgment. Twice the world is arithmetic designed to break negotiation. Wealth that bought protection, labour, food, and honour becomes a single plotted offer to buy back a soul. The verse lets greed run to its maximum and still shows it arriving underfunded, because the owner never truly owned the assets brought as his ransom.

phrases.translation: they would certainly offer it to ransom themselves.
phrases.explanation: They would ransom themselves with it tells us the desire behind the hypothetical fortune. At the sight of consequence no person calculates a discount for family monuments or national projects. Everything becomes price. The sentence is a warning to use possessions before the market closes through charity, justice, and repentance while hands can still release them freely. A fortune spent toward God in life can become a companion, guarding it as an alternative lord cannot.

phrases.translation: They will face strict judgment, and Hell will be their home. What an evil place to rest
phrases.explanation: Evil reckoning and Hell as refuge or resting place ends the ransom hope with exact accounting. A bad reckoning means no deed is overlooked in the way a merciful easy reckoning may pass over faults for a believer. Refuge sounds bitter here because the place reached at the end of escape attempts is the punishment itself. What a terrible bed or cradle uses domestic language to make permanence feel personal rather than abstract.

phrases.translation: Can the one who knows that your Lord’s revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ is the truth be like the one who is blind?
phrases.explanation: Can one who knows revelation to you is truth be like one who is blind asks whether recognition and refusal can be equal. The knowing person in early application may be Muhammad or any believer whose sight rests on certainty, set against a denier pictured through blindness. Blindness here is refusal to let evidence become sight rather than a comment on bodily disability. The question forms the doorway into a portrait of people whose intelligence has moral depth.

phrases.translation: None will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.explanation: Only people of deep intellect remember gives those portraits an entry condition. A deep intellect in the verse language reaches the core rather than skimming the husk of a sign. Remembrance is active conversion of knowledge into covenant, kinship, patience, prayer, and generosity over the next verses. The Quran therefore defines intelligence by what remembered truth does to a life. A clever arguer can remain blind while an unlettered believer sees the road and walks it.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who honour Allah’s covenant, never breaking the pledge
phrases.explanation: Those who fulfil Allah covenant and do not break the firm agreement begin the portrait with loyalty over time. Covenant can include the primordial and revealed commitments accepted by a believer, then every promise governed by them. Not breaking is harder than making a pledge at a moving moment. It survives boredom, fear, changing company, and opportunities to profit by revision. The deep mind promised in the prior verse first becomes visible as fidelity.

phrases.translation: and those who maintain whatever ˹ties˺ Allah has ordered to be maintained, stand in awe of their Lord, and fear strict judgment
phrases.explanation: Joining what Allah commanded to be joined widens covenant loyalty into kinship, community, revelation, and every rightful bond that anger or greed may want severed. They fear their Lord and dread an evil reckoning, so family repair is worship rather than public relations. A person might maintain prayer while cutting parents and neighbours from the heart. This verse refuses that split. The road to the final home is paved through kept relationships.

phrases.translation: And ˹they are˺ those who endure patiently, seeking their Lord’s pleasure,
phrases.explanation: Patience seeking the face or pleasure of their Lord supplies the motive that keeps endurance from becoming performance for applause. A patient person can be praised by a crowd while inwardly defeated by the wish to be seen. Seeking Allah face points the same waiting toward divine acceptance. In a chapter of rain and foam, patience is the valley capacity that lets a person carry more truth without spilling it at the first storm.

phrases.translation: establish prayer, donate from what We have provided for them—secretly and openly—and respond to evil with good.
phrases.explanation: Establish prayer, spend secretly and openly from provision, and repel evil with good gives patience daily institutions. Secret giving purifies intention while open giving can teach and supply public need, and each guards the other from vanity or cowardice. Repelling evil with good may mean kindness for insult, forgiveness where possible, and lawful action that refuses imitation. The portrait becomes social enough that a neighbourhood would notice these people before their final home is mentioned.

phrases.translation: It is they who will have the ultimate abode
phrases.explanation: The final outcome of the home belongs to such people, a phrase that treats Paradise as the settling of a journey rather than a surprise prize. Home has been threatened throughout prophetic history by exile, prison, market, storm, and broken families. Ultimate home means no later landlord, flood, accusation, or grave will reverse the address. The verse slows the speed of a moral list so the reader can taste where kept covenants and secret charity are travelling.

phrases.translation: the Gardens of Eternity, which they will enter along with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants.
phrases.explanation: Gardens of Eden entered with righteous parents, spouses, and descendants makes salvation communal without turning ancestry into a ticket. Only those who were righteous among family are gathered, so kinship adds joy after individual faith has done its work. Separation is one of earth deepest wounds, and this promise answers it by reunion at a higher level. The household joins what God commanded to be joined now receives its eternal form.

phrases.translation: And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, ˹saying,˺
phrases.explanation: Angels enter from every door turns the garden residence into a visited home rather than beautiful isolation. Every door suggests completeness of welcome and no back entrance of shame. The visitors arrive with the sentence that will explain the honour. In worldly palaces important people enter through guarded doors while servants slip by side passages. Here heaven attendants move freely toward former strugglers whose names may have mattered to almost nobody outside a small street.

phrases.translation: “Peace be upon you for your perseverance. How excellent is the ultimate abode!”
phrases.explanation: Peace be upon you for your patience makes endurance the inscription on the gate. The greeting does not say peace because your life was easy or because your family was powerful. It identifies the road by which they carried covenant, prayer, generosity, and non retaliation through storms. How excellent the final home gives the travellers an evaluation from angels who know both worlds. The verse teaches earth patience to listen ahead for the sound at the door.

phrases.translation: And those who violate Allah’s covenant after it has been affirmed,
phrases.explanation: Breaking Allah covenant after its confirmation reverses the first quality of the saved group and adds deliberateness to the failure. A covenant can be confirmed by innate witness, revelation, oath, and acceptance, so breaking it is not confusion at the starting line. The verse begins the opposite portrait without changing literary key. Covenants are the roads on which a person either reaches the final home or constructs a different destination deed by deed.

phrases.translation: break whatever ˹ties˺ Allah has ordered to be maintained, and spread corruption in the land—
phrases.explanation: Cutting what Allah commanded to be joined and corrupting on earth turns a private breach into social breakage. Family ties, prophetic bonds, neighbour rights, and public trusts can all be cut by people whose first loyalty has collapsed. Corruption spreads because every severed bond forces someone else to carry cost. The rain parable now has a human form, since foam also rides on useful water for a while and leaves damage in its glittering wake.

phrases.translation: it is they who will be condemned and will have the worst abode
phrases.explanation: A curse and an evil home answer the promise of peace at every door with distance from mercy and a ruined final address. Curse here means being placed far from the good they refused to join. The parallel is exact enough to teach by architecture. One company receives angels at the doors. The other receives a home whose main quality is that mercy has been kept away by the life built inside it.

phrases.translation: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Allah expands provision for whom He wills and measures it out makes wealth an unreliable certificate of truth. A shop can widen through talent, timing, inheritance, exploitation, or divine permission, so income alone cannot settle whose theology heaven approves. Measure returns from the womb verse and applies to rice, coins, health, and lifespan. The reader is warned against letting a bank balance preach a sermon the Quran never gave it.

phrases.translation: And the disbelievers become prideful of ˹the pleasures of˺ this worldly life.
phrases.explanation: They rejoice in worldly life describes a celebration limited to what can be consumed inside a short season. Rejoicing itself is not forbidden, since gratitude can rejoice and charity can widen a table. The danger is a joy that stops at acquisition and becomes proof that denial was wise. Foam also rises quickly and catches light. A loud surface can make an audience forget that water underneath will decide what remains.

phrases.translation: But the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is nothing but a fleeting enjoyment
phrases.explanation: Worldly life beside the Hereafter is only a brief enjoyment gives scale without calling food, homes, tools, and family worthless. Brief frames duration, because even a hundred harvests narrow to a handbreadth beside forever. A person can honour useful metal and rain while refusing to make them the final residence. The verse sits between two portraits of homes, teaching provision to serve the journey rather than impersonate the destination.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “If only a sign could be sent down to him from his Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Why is no sign sent down to him from his Lord repeats the demand from verse seven after the entire parable of valleys and foam. Repetition now performs its own diagnosis, because the audience has been handed exactly the sort of sign that explains why additional spectacle may not settle the heart. A bigger flood still requires a valley to receive it. Their request reveals an instrument problem they would rather assign to heaven communications office.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, Allah leaves to stray whoever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him—
phrases.explanation: Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whoever turns back places sovereignty and human turning in one difficult sentence. Early theology kept divine will inside justice and the record of refusal rather than arbitrary diversion from innocence. Turning back is therefore the human door named in the same breath. A person begging for one more sign can begin by turning with the signs already in hand, because guidance often recognises a face that has started moving home.

phrases.translation: those who believe and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and whose hearts are calmed by Allah remembrance describes the turning people from the inside. Calm does not mean absence of grief, danger, poverty, or argument in the chapter. It means the heart has a settled address for fear and hope during weather. A valley at peace still receives floodwater, yet its banks know a direction. Belief becomes emotional geography rather than only a statement approved at a public meeting.

phrases.translation: Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort
phrases.explanation: Surely by remembrance of Allah hearts are calmed repeats the core with a certainty many readers use as a daily medicine. Remembrance includes Quran recitation, prayer, names of God, gratitude, and mindful return in ordinary work. It does not promise that a sentence will erase a diagnosis or an enemy by lunchtime. It promises a centre that pain cannot easily evict. In a chapter of thunder, the loudest sound is answered by a stilled heart.

phrases.translation: Those who believe and do good, for them will be bliss and an honourable destination.”
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds receive Tuba and a beautiful return, a word early commentators explained as supreme bliss, a tree in Paradise, or every form of good gathered into one name. Holding those readings together enriches rather than burdens the verse. Good deeds take root in the world like the lasting metal and water. Their shade is promised in the next, and the road home itself becomes beautiful because of the One receiving them.

phrases.translation: And so We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ to a community,
phrases.explanation: Thus We sent you to a community before whom other communities passed places Muhammad inside a procession rather than a surprise event. His audience can study earlier responses to messengers and locate themselves before their own period ends. A new community is not a new moral universe. Its markets may differ from Midian and its idols from Egypt, yet envy, demand for signs, haste, and gratitude or rebellion repeat in familiar accents.

phrases.translation: like ˹We did with˺ earlier communities, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you.
phrases.explanation: That you may recite what We revealed makes delivery the core of sending before political outcomes enter. A recited book can work slowly through households and generations in ways a single spectacle cannot store. The sentence consoles the Prophet by defining success at the level of faithful transmission. Communities before his also heard messages that outlived immediate rejection. A voice at a doorway can become history curriculum when people finally decide to listen.

phrases.translation: Yet they deny the Most Compassionate. Say, “He is my Lord!
phrases.explanation: Yet they disbelieve in the Most Merciful turns a name of compassion into the rejected identity of the sender. Denial is not always framed as rejecting an angry abstraction. People can resist the Lord precisely as universal mercy challenges their need for tribal mediators and negotiable gods. Saying He is my Lord starts Muhammad answer with personal allegiance rather than a theory about their motives. The rejected name becomes his address.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. In Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn ˹in repentance˺.”
phrases.explanation: No god except Him, on Him I trust, and to Him is my return gathers worship, reliance, and repentance into a compact creed after rejection. Return here can carry turning back in daily repentance and final return in judgment, allowing both horizons to steady conduct. The Prophet does not promise to force the city into agreement. He states the centre from which his patience will operate while time and signs continue their work.

phrases.translation: If there were a recitation that could cause mountains to move,
phrases.explanation: If there were a Quran by which mountains moved imagines revelation physically bulldozing the landscape in the form deniers claim to require. Mountains have been stabilising signs since verse three, so moving them would be a seizure of the familiar world. The hypothetical tests whether spectacle itself creates submission. Scripture usually aims to move hearts before geography, and a mountain carried across a valley could still leave a council negotiating the meaning of dust.

phrases.translation: or the earth to split, or the dead to speak, ˹it would have been this Quran˺.
phrases.explanation: Earth split or dead spoken to completes the catalogue of wonders that would satisfy some definitions of proof. A speaking corpse sounds conclusive until the living begin classifying it as magic, ventriloquism, political theatre, or a temporary event. The suppressed conclusion in many readings is that even such a Quran would not mechanically produce faith. Every sign still needs an audience willing to stop calling the valley too small and the water unclear.

phrases.translation: But all matters are by Allah’s Will. Have the believers not yet realized that had Allah willed, He could have guided all of humanity?
phrases.explanation: Rather to Allah belongs the affair entirely stops the negotiation over customised miracles. Have believers not despaired or learned that God could guide all humanity if He willed addresses the ache of preachers who wonder why universal compulsion is withheld. Translation of the key verb has been discussed between despairing of their belief and knowing the divine possibility. Either direction reaches surrender about mass outcomes while continuing local invitation.

phrases.translation: And disasters will continue to afflict the disbelievers or strike close to their homes for their misdeeds, until Allah’s promise comes to pass.
phrases.explanation: Disasters will keep striking deniers or landing near their home for deeds until Allah promise arrives describes history as a sequence of warnings at and around the address. A calamity nearby can teach without consuming the hearer, giving time to connect conduct and consequence. The verse should not be used to label every sufferer a particular sinner. It presents revealed knowledge about communities under warning and commands humility when trouble passes close enough to be heard through the wall.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah never fails in His promise
phrases.explanation: Allah does not break the appointment gives patience a schedule even when the date is hidden. An appointment kept in heaven may look late from a market that wants either instant punishment or instant vindication. Certainty about arrival changes how a believer handles the middle. Mockery can borrow confidence from one quiet week. The verse returns the calendar to a Lord whose delay is governed by the same measure that governs wombs and rain.

phrases.translation: Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you, but I delayed the disbelievers ˹for a while˺ then seized them. And how ˹horrible˺ was My punishment
phrases.explanation: Messengers before you were mocked and I granted respite to deniers then seized them compresses many of the stories already heard into one consolation. Mockery is an old professional hazard rather than proof that a new prophet has failed at public relations. Respite makes the middle dangerous for interpreters because laughter can look successful while the term runs. How was My punishment asks readers to remember the final grammar of Pharaoh, destroyed towns, and drowned armies before judging the current delay.

phrases.translation: Is ˹there any equal to˺ the Vigilant One Who knows what every soul commits?
phrases.explanation: Is the One standing over every soul with what it earns like a partner that cannot answer makes vigilance the test of divinity. Standing over in classical language suggests watchful management in which no request, intention, wage, or sin leaves the record. A god that must be carried to a festival cannot stand over the carrier in this sense. The unanswered comparison asks hearers to give up a tie their habits pretend exists.

phrases.translation: Yet the pagans have associated others with Allah ˹in worship˺.
phrases.explanation: Yet they made associates for Allah records behaviour continuing in defiance of the comparison they just failed to answer. Association can be maintained by processions, inherited names, vows, and fear of social rupture after the intellectual case has ended. The word yet carries exasperation because custom can outlive its own argument. People may lose a debate in the morning and attend the shrine by evening because belonging has not yet changed its address.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Name them! Or do you ˹mean to˺ inform Him of something He does not know on the earth?
phrases.explanation: Name them demands the partners be identified with attributes rather than hidden behind festival atmosphere. Or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth turns an invented pantheon into a report supposedly delivered upward to omniscience. If such beings had a real share in divinity, the Knower would not need a worshipper press release. The question strips mystery language down to a request for credentials no associate can produce.

phrases.translation: Or are these ˹gods˺ just empty words?” In fact, the disbelievers’ falsehood has been made so appealing to them that they have been turned away from the Path.
phrases.explanation: Or is it only outward speech suggests their case consists of pronounceable names with no corresponding authority, much like the water held away from the mouth. Their scheme has been made attractive and they have been barred from the path shows decoration doing the work evidence could not. A procession can make a hollow title sound full for an afternoon. The verse traces false worship from title, to ritual beauty, to a blocked road a person mistakes for heritage.

phrases.translation: And whoever Allah leaves to stray will be left with no guide
phrases.explanation: Whoever Allah leads astray has no guide closes the route around a final rejected condition while preserving the chapter pattern that guidance meets the one who turns. No alternative guide can be hired from among the named partners because their silence was the problem at the start. The sentence warns against enjoying decorated error until correction begins to sound like noise. A guide requires sight, answer, and authority, and the contest over those qualities has already been held.

phrases.translation: For them is punishment in this worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is truly far worse.
phrases.explanation: Punishment in worldly life can include disgrace, loss, disaster, fear, and the slow consequences revealed through the stories, while punishment in the Hereafter is harder because it settles what earth only sampled. A near calamity in the earlier verse belongs to this first category when revelation interprets it. The comparison should produce urgency without encouraging spectators to diagnose every private pain. Its clear use is prophetic warning to persistent deniers gathered around the message.

phrases.translation: And none can shield them from Allah
phrases.explanation: No shield from Allah removes the last imagined use of partners, tribe, wealth, or public numbers at the final court. A shield only works if it can stand between a person and a stronger force. The associates have already failed benefit, harm, creation, response, and guidance tests. The sentence quietly completes the equipment check. At judgment there will be no object to hide behind because every candidate is part of the creation being judged.

phrases.translation: The description of the Paradise promised to the righteous is that under it rivers flow; eternal is its fruit as well as its shade.
phrases.explanation: The likeness of Paradise promised to the mindful has rivers under it and fruit and shade that never fail, returning the water imagery with its foam removed. Earthly valleys carry useful flow for a season while orchards lose fruit and shade moves or thins. Perpetuity is the difference between a picnic and a home. Mindful people are promised an environment where the good that benefits does not have to be separated again from glittering waste.

phrases.translation: That is the ˹ultimate˺ outcome for the righteous. But the outcome for the disbelievers is the Fire
phrases.explanation: That is the outcome of the mindful and the outcome of disbelievers is Fire sets two destinations in one visual line. Outcome has been the governing word behind homes, processions, ransom, towns, and messengers. The verse gives no third neutral address where a person can admire rivers from outside while refusing the covenant road. Its brevity is part of its force because the entire chapter machinery has been moving people toward one of these two settlements.

phrases.translation: ˹The believers among˺ those who were given the Scripture rejoice at what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺,
phrases.explanation: Those given the Book rejoice in what was sent to Muhammad introduces a believing response from earlier scripture communities, commonly linked with sincere Jewish and Christian converts or readers who recognised continuity. Rejoicing matters because possession of an older Book does not always produce rivalry. A reader can greet a later confirmation with relief when party identity has not become more sacred than truth. Their joy becomes an external sign that revelation need not sound foreign to its own history.

phrases.translation: while some ˹disbelieving˺ factions deny a portion of it.
phrases.explanation: Some factions deny part of it gives the less tidy response, where group interest accepts convenient overlap and rejects claims that challenge local authority. Portion denial can look moderate while still letting the faction sit as editor over a messenger. Factions may include Arab idolaters and scripture parties in various explanations. The verse does not flatten every reader of previous Books into one camp. It sorts by conduct toward the truth that has arrived.

phrases.translation: Say, “I have only been commanded to worship Allah, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.
phrases.explanation: Say, I was only commanded to worship Allah without associating any partner gives Muhammad a non negotiable centre amid partial acceptance. A prophet might be tempted to build a coalition by softening the exact verses each faction dislikes. Only commanded sets the limit of political flexibility before hospitality begins. The statement also recalls Joseph in prison, because the same refusal to split worship can be spoken in a cell or before learned communities.

phrases.translation: To Him I invite ˹all˺, and to Him is my return.”
phrases.explanation: To Him I call and to Him is my return makes invitation and destination identical in direction. A caller who points elsewhere for final safety would split the message at its root. Return gives the Prophet personal stake in the worship he commands others to enter. The verse responds to selective acceptance with wholeness, since a road that leads back to God cannot be cut into party approved segments without losing its arrival.

phrases.translation: And so We have revealed it as an authority in Arabic.
phrases.explanation: Thus We sent it down as an Arabic judgment or authoritative recitation presents the Quran as decision in the first audience language. Arabic removes the excuse that a foreign code must be mediated before conscience can move. Judgment also means the Book is meant to settle disputes rather than provide decorative spirituality. Earlier scripture communities, Arab tribes, and later translators all meet a text whose clarity carries responsibility across their boundaries.

phrases.translation: And if you were to follow their desires after ˹all˺ the knowledge that has come to you,
phrases.explanation: If you follow their desires after knowledge has come gives Muhammad a direct border against coalition editing. Desires are not every human preference in food or custom. They are pressures to alter worship and message for acceptance. Knowledge already received raises the cost of surrender because a person who has seen the road cannot plead fog with honesty. The hypothetical keeps leadership humble enough to fear a wrong step even while heaven protects the mission.

phrases.translation: there would be none to protect or shield you from Allah
phrases.explanation: No guardian or shield from Allah would remain if that border were crossed makes the warning universal through its highest addressee. Even a prophet cannot use office as a barrier after exchanging clear knowledge for audience desire. The sentence closes a possible loophole while comforting ordinary believers that God judgment does not run on celebrity access. Authority increases accountability because the one carrying the sign knows where the sign points.

phrases.translation: We have certainly sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ and blessed them with wives and offspring.
phrases.explanation: Messengers before you were given wives and descendants answers the recurring expectation that a heavenly messenger should stand outside ordinary family life. Marriage and children place prophets inside kitchens, inheritances, illnesses, grief, and local obligations. That humanity makes their patience imitable and their suffering intelligible. The verse also protects Muhammad domestic life from being used as evidence against revelation by people who imagine holiness must look detached from the species it came to guide.

phrases.translation: It was not for any messenger to bring a sign without Allah’s permission.
phrases.explanation: No messenger could bring a sign except by Allah permission returns the wonder schedule to the sender. A prophet may plead, warn, work, and wait, yet the public sign that ends an argument is not a tool in his pocket. Permission language preserves the freedom and wisdom of God while protecting the messenger from becoming a performer under contract. Audiences who keep raising the price of belief must negotiate with heaven, not a technician.

phrases.translation: Every destined matter has a ˹set˺ time
phrases.explanation: For every term there is a writing makes time itself a document rather than empty delay. Births, deaths, rains, kingdoms, revelations, punishments, and rescues each meet a page on which their boundary is already known. The statement gives the Prophet a way to endure the gap between promise and event. A book in heaven is more stable than the mood of a crowd trying to decide whether this week counts as evidence.

phrases.translation: Allah eliminates and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Master Record
phrases.explanation: Allah erases what He wills and confirms, with the Mother of the Book beside Him, has generated rich discussion about records of deeds, terms, provisions, abrogation, and angels registers. A careful reading can hold the common structure without forcing one application to consume all others. What changes in a documented order does so by the Author will, while the master source remains secure beyond human editing. Delay and alteration therefore do not mean heaven has lost the file.

phrases.translation: Whether We show you ˹O Prophet˺ some of what We threaten them with,
phrases.explanation: Whether We show you part of what they are promised or take you in death frees Muhammad from needing to witness every consequence in his own lifetime. Part matters because vindication may arrive in stages through conversion, defeat, exposure, or social change before final judgment. A messenger can die with work apparently unfinished and still have completed his assignment. Joseph cupbearer and the destroyed towns both taught readers that a generation is a small window inside a longer record.

phrases.translation: or cause you to die ˹before that˺, your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. Judgment is for Us
phrases.explanation: Your duty is only delivery and on Us is reckoning divides labour between prophet and Lord with pastoral clarity. Delivery requires courage, clarity, patience, and non editing under desire. Reckoning requires perfect knowledge and authority no human court possesses. This division can let a preacher sleep without surrendering urgency. The message goes out completely. The sorting of every hearer remains with the One who heard secret and public speech exactly alike.

phrases.translation: Do they not see that We gradually reduce their land from its borders?
phrases.explanation: Have they not seen We come to the land reducing it from its edges uses a moving map as a sign while arguments continue. Early readings connected the shrinking with Muslim expansion taking surrounding territory, deaths of leaders, loss of produce, or towns falling one by one. Preserving those applications shows a pattern rather than a single snapshot. A confident centre should notice its border being educated before the lesson reaches its own street.

phrases.translation: Allah decides—none can reverse His decision. And He is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: Allah judges and none can reverse His judgment gives the changing map a court above military and political weather. A decision from God is not sent to a council of partners for appeal. Swift in reckoning adds speed when the appointed settling starts, answering people who mistake long delay for administrative difficulty. The Judge who waits by measure can close an account without needing centuries to locate the record.

phrases.translation: Those ˹disbelievers˺ before them ˹secretly˺ planned, but Allah has the ultimate plan.
phrases.explanation: Those before them plotted, yet all plotting belongs to Allah returns human schemes to the scale learned from Joseph. A person can plan a pit, a banquet, a prison term, a false shirt, or a public sign demand. None of those moves escapes the larger conduct of affairs named at the chapter opening. Plots remain morally owned by their makers, while their final use can be turned into rescue, evidence, or judgment by God wisdom.

phrases.translation: He knows what every soul commits. And the disbelievers will soon know who will have the ultimate outcome
phrases.explanation: He knows what every soul earns and disbelievers will know who has the final home brings private accounting and public destination into one promise. Present argument can award itself the title of winner after every gathering. Final home will require a different language. The verse speaks to Muhammad in the cadence of Shuaib and Joseph, asking him to let time finish sentences that mockers try to close with laughter.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “You ˹Muḥammad˺ are no messenger.” Say, ˹O Prophet,
phrases.explanation: Disbelievers say you are not a messenger gives the whole conflict its blunt final form after signs, parables, previous nations, scripture witnesses, and changing borders. The sentence is not asking for one more exhibit. It rejects the office itself. Say introduces an answer that does not chase every objection into a new arena. At some point a prophet names the witness competent to settle a case the audience keeps reopening for social reasons.

phrases.translation: ˺ “Allah is sufficient as a Witness between me and you,
phrases.explanation: Allah suffices as witness between me and you returns the dispute to the Knower of unseen and witnessed from the opening movement. Sufficiency means the case does not collapse when a crowd refuses the role of fair jury. A witness who saw revelation, intention, private plots, public delivery, and every refusal can close what debate leaves tangled. The Prophet hands his identity to the highest court rather than renting it from applause.

phrases.translation: as is whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.”
phrases.explanation: Whoever has knowledge of the Book as another witness has been explained as a learned believer from earlier scripture, the community of such witnesses, or in some readings with an even wider reference carefully discussed by commentators. The verse should not be forced into one biography where tradition carried several. Its narrative force is clear. Revelation does not stand without recognition among people trained to read its predecessors, and God witness remains sufficient above every human endorsement.
